events.description:
A three-round competition testing strategic thinking, problem-solving, and analytical skills.

Round 1: Brain Buster Blitz (Quiz Round)
Teams will tackle a quiz filled with challenging questions. Both members collaborate, and their combined performance will determine advancement.

Round 2: The Riddle Conundrum
Teams must solve 5 riddles in the shortest time possible. Those solving the most riddles in the least time advance.

Round 3: Strategic Mastermind (Case Study Presentation)
5–7 min to present, another 5 min for the question-answer round.
1. Teams will be assigned a common case study focused on strategy formulation.
2. They will have 10–12 minutes (5–7 min presentation + 5 min Q&A). Performance will be judged on strategic and analytical skills.
3. Judges will ask questions for evaluation.
rules: Round 1: Brain Buster Blitz (Quiz Round) — both team members collaborate on a quiz of challenging questions, and their combined performance determines advancement.
Round 2: The Riddle Conundrum — teams solve 5 riddles in the shortest possible time. Teams solving the most riddles in the least time advance.
Round 3: Strategic Mastermind (Case Study Presentation) — teams are assigned a common case study focused on strategy formulation.
Teams have 10–12 minutes in total: 5–7 minutes for the presentation and 5 minutes for questions and answers.
Performance is judged on strategic and analytical skills, and judges ask questions for evaluation.

events.description:
The participants will be given 2 minutes to introduce themselves, followed by some leadership questions. (This will not be an elimination round.)

Round 1: Parichaya (Introduction)
The participants will be given 2 minutes to introduce themselves, followed by some leadership questions. (This will not be an elimination round.)

Round 2: Vaad-Vivad (Debate)
Participants will be provided with a current topic and will be required to actively participate by clearly stating their stance, without contradicting themselves. Topics will be disclosed at the time of the debate, and this round will test an individual’s spontaneity and persuasiveness.

Round 3: Vaktavya (Elocution)
Participants will be provided with a topic for the elocution. After the monologue, the audience or the judges will ask questions based on the content of the speech given by the participant.
rules: Round 1: Parichaya (Introduction) — participants receive 2 minutes to introduce themselves, followed by leadership questions. This is not an elimination round.
Round 2: Vaad-Vivad (Debate) — participants receive a current topic and must actively participate by clearly presenting their stance without contradicting themselves.
Debate topics are disclosed at the time of the round, which tests spontaneity and persuasiveness.
Round 3: Vaktavya (Elocution) — participants receive an elocution topic, followed by questions from the audience or judges based on the content of the speech.

events.description:
Stall Mart is a two-round competition where participants will showcase their creativity, business acumen, and organizational skills by setting up and managing stalls. The event tests ideation, execution, and revenue generation skills.

Round 1: Idea Sprint
Teams will present their stall concept and strategy in a concise and clear manner, explaining the products or services offered and how they plan to attract customers.

Round 2: The Entrepreneur’s Arena
Teams will set up and manage their stalls based on their proposed ideas. Stalls can feature artistic creations, games with psychological themes, food, etc. Teams must keep their stalls tidy and organized.

Evaluation will be based on revenue generated, productivity, and a task assigned by the Event Coordinators (ECs).
rules: No gambling games, events or any objectionable subjects.
Only the members of the participating team are allowed in the stall.
No unfair means will be tolerated.
Stalls will be allotted on a first-come, first-served basis.
An everyday balance sheet will have to be maintained.
